The king was glad, and he and his people were
more hopeful than they had ever been before.
When night came, the king lay awake for a long
time, and thought about the things that had hap-
pened that day. At last he fancied that he saw
a great light like the sun; and in the midst of the
light there stood an old man with black hair, hold-
ing an open book in his hand.
It may all have been a dream, and yet to the king
it seemed very real indeed. He looked and won-
dered, but was not afraid.

Each Campfire group meets once a
week. When the weather permits,
meetings will be held out-of-doors
and the regular camp work will be
begun.
Automobile Fractures Banker’s Wrist.
C. B. Bowling, president of the Ex-
change National Bank, is suffering
today from a broken wrist, which was
injured Friday evening when he was
cranking an automobile. The injury
is not severe. Mr. Bowling was out
of the house a short time yesterday.
Prof. Stephens at Assembly.
Prof. F. F. Stephens will speak at
7:15 o’clock Tuesday night at the last
Assembly at the University before
Easter on “The Monroe Doctrine—Its
Development, Interpretation and In-
ternational Significance.”
